REPORT DATE: 06-29-2021 REPORT TIME: 1500 UTC REGION: ATLANTIC SUB REGION: SOUTHEAST U.S. AREA/BLOCK: N/A IMAGE DATE: 06-28-2021 IMAGE TIME: 2320 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL1A MODE: INTERFEROMETRIC WIDE (IW) VV RESOLUTION: 20 METER LOCATION: 26°29"11" N/79°23"38" W AREA: 12.27 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY OCCURRED JUST OUTSIDE OF THE US EEZ, EXTENDED ABOUT 12 NM LONG BY AROUND 0.5 NM WIDE AT ITS WIDEST POINT, HAD GOOD CONTRAST WITH ITS BACKGROUND AND HAD UNNATURAL KINKS AND TURNS. ALTHOUGH SOME CHARACTERISTICS OF THE ANOMALY WERE CONSISTENT WITH A BILGE DUMP, OTHER TRAITS SUCH AS FEATHERING AND DISCRETE WIDENING WITH DISTANCE WERE NOT OBSERVED IN A MAJORITY OF THE ANOMALY. ADDITIONALLY, ALTHOUGH VESSELS WERE IN THE SCENE, THEY DO NOT APPEAR RELATED TO THE ANOMALY. WINDS AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE SE AT 5-10 KT. CONSIDERING THE ABOVE FACTORS, WE HAVE MEDIUM-HIGH CONFIDENCE IN THIS ASSESSMENT. UNCERTAINTIES: THE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE ANOMALY DID NOT MEET ALL THE CLASSIC HALLMARKS OF A BILGE DUMP.

Report DescriptionPOTENTIAL DISCHARGE OF GASOLINE FROM A 29 FT WELL CRAFT COASTAL THAT HIT A PATCH OF SEAWEED CAUSING THE MOTOR TO STOP AND A WAVE PUSHED THE VESSEL AGROUND. THERE WAS ALSO DAMAGE TO THE VESSEL. IT IS UNKNOWN HOW MUCH GASOLINE WAS ONBOARD THE VESSEL BUT THE CAPACITY IS 225 GALLONS. SEATOW WAS ONSCENE AND A TOW COMPANY WAS HIRED. THE VESSEL WAS TAKEN OUT OF THE WATER BUT THERE IS STILL ACTION TO BE TAKEN TO REMOVE THE VESSEL THROUGH THE BEACH SIDE. CALLER STATES THE AREA WHERE THE INCIDENT TOOK PLACE IS A NESTING GROUND FOR SEA TURTLES (WHICH ARE PROTECTED) BUT THERE IS A VOLUNTEER GROUP (WHO WORK WITH THE STATE) TO ASSIST WITH MITIGATING ANY IMPACT TO THE TURTLES WHILE THEY REMOVE THE VESSEL. CALLER STATES THEY DO NOT KNOW HOW FAR OUT OF THE WATER THE VESSEL HAS BEEN TAKEN AT THIS TIME.

properties.content:

Nearest City: Evart, MI
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: HYDRAULIC OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: VENTRA EVART, LLC
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 25 gallons
HYDRAULIC OIL DISCHARGED TO A LINE RETENTION POND FROM A HEAT EXCHANGER. MUCH OF THE RELEASE WAS CONTAINED IN THE POND, BUT A SLIGHT SHEEN WAS OBSERVED AT THE OUTFALL AT THE MUSKEGON RIVER. THE SOURCE HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AND ISOLATED. ACCORDING TO THE MDSM, THE MATERIAL IS INHERENTLY BIODEGRADABLE, NOT HARMFUL TO AQUATIC ORGANISMS, AND RCRA NON-HAZADROUS. THE RELEASE WAS CONFINED WITH BOOMS AND REMOVED USING SUITABLE ABSORBENTS CONSISTENT WITH THE MSDS. ALL HYDRAULIC PRESSES WERE TESTED FOR LEAK DETECTION. A SAMPLE OF THE RETENTION POND WATER WAS ANALYZED AND POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED AS HYDRAULIC OIL. NO OTHER CONSTITUENTS WERE FOUND IN THE EPA-CERTIFIED ANALYSIS. AFFECTED WATER FROM THE POND WAS PUMPED OUT AND HAULED OFF SITE FOR TREATMENT/DISPOSAL.

Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
UPON ARRIVAL AT CUSTOMER'S FARM, FUEL DELIVERY DRIVER PRESET DIGITAL METER FOR DELIVERY OF 100 GALLONS OF OFFROAD DIESEL IN CUSTOMER'S 300 GALLON AST. DRIVER COMMENCED DISPENSING OPERATION, THEN WALKED AWAY FROM THE NOZZLE TO SPEAK WITH THE CUSTOMER IN THE BARN. CUSTOMER'S WIFE ALERTED DRIVER THAT FUEL WAS RUNNING ON THE GROUND. DRIVER RAN TO TANK TRUCK, STOPPED PUMP, THEN IMMEDIATELY STARTED SPILL RESPONSE PROCEDURES SETTING OUT ABSORBENT PADS AND A BOOM TO CONTAIN THE SPILL TO MINIMIZE THE SPREAD OF FUEL. HE THEN CALLED DISPATCH WHO INITIATED RESPONSE FOR A SPILL CLEAN UP, AND THEN HE RETURNED TO SPILL CONTAINMENT UNTIL HELP ARRIVED. CONTRACTOR RESPONDED WITH EQUIPMENT INCLUDING A VAC TRAILER TO CAPTURE POOLED FREE PRODUCT. A SECOND CONTRACTOR, ALSO CALLED TO RESPOND, TESTED AND OVERSAW THE REMOVAL OF DIESEL FUEL CONTAMINATED SOILS.
